comments.note: _derive_next_action helper, line ~130: 'elif re == "FAIL": next_role, action = "Developer", "REWORK"' diverges from the manifest. The manifest fail_routing specifies release-engineering → release_engineer → "Release Engineer", not "Developer". This contrasts correctly with sa/cr which both manifest-route to developer. No existing test exercises this path through the helper (TestDirectActionRouting bypasses the helper via direct injection), so there is no false assertion today. However the helper's own drift-risk docstring warns exactly about this class of divergence. A future test author who adds a re.FAIL scenario using _derive_next_action would get a misleading assertion. Fix: change the branch to 'next_role, action = "Release Engineer", "REWORK"'.

TestDirectActionRouting is missing a REWORK case for Release Engineer (by analogy with the Developer REWORK case). TestDirectActionRouting tests direct action dispatch, which is production code. If a 'REWORK' action is ever returned for a Release Engineer role, the supervisor would route to release_engineer — but this is untested. Minor gap given REWORK-to-RE is currently only exercised via helper scenarios, not direct injection.
